_format: extraction answer key v2 — hand-labelled ground truth for one document
_changes_from_v1: v1 (BetterVet) described a single-vaccination certificate. This page is a portal
summary: an eleven-row table where most rows are NOT vaccines. Three sections are
new because this document needs them and v1 did not:
line_items[]          — every row, classified. v1's 'vaccinations[]' assumed the
page only contained vaccinations. This one does not, and
vocabulary_decisions[] — terms that require a human mapping the first time they
are seen, and what the correct mapping is.
schema_gaps[]         — facts this page carries that the database currently has
nowhere to put. A key that only checks extraction misses
absent.unfilled_form_fields — a third category of absence that v1 did not need.
Keep v1's three assertions: expected / absent / must_not_produce.
_format_family_note: Petly is a portal product (Covetrus/IDEXX) used by many clinics, so this layout will recur across DIFFERENT practices. That makes it a high-value format family: one labelled example covers every Petly clinic, unlike a practice-specific invoice layout.
_doc_class_problem: See schema_gaps[1]. This is neither an invoice nor a rabies certificate, and document_class has no value that fits. It falls to 'unknown', which is wrong in a way that matters — the confidence you should place in a field depends on what kind of document it came from.
_mime_note: Not 'application/jpg'. document.mime_type has a CHECK constraint allowing only application/pdf, image/jpeg, image/png, image/heic. 'application/jpg' fails the insert.

capture_quality.medium: screenshot of a web page, not a generated PDF
_implications: No text layer. OCR is required, unlike the three PDFs, so this document exercises a different failure surface — character confusion rather than field misattribution.

The page is cropped at the right edge: the header link reads '<< back to your pet's pag' with the final character cut off. Truncated tokens at image boundaries are an OCR artifact, not a fact about the document.
The same screenshot was uploaded twice. Byte-identical files under one owner collide on UNIQUE (owner_id, sha256) — the intended behaviour, and worth an explicit test.

_pii._why: Anonymised at labelling time. Clinical facts (dates, product names) are kept verbatim so the key can be checked against the page.
_preserve_the_structure: This dog's owner is a DIFFERENT household from the Jaddi documents. Give the two
owners different surnames in the pseudonyms. A shared surname would quietly
invent a household linkage that does not exist, and every test built on this
fixture would then be exercising the wrong case. Anonymisation has to preserve
the relationships you intend to test, not just remove the names.
_pii._identifiers: Microchip and rabies tag are strong identifiers and are substituted here. Keep the real-to-pseudonym mapping outside version control — reconciling the same dog across two clinics later depends on it.

patient.name: Luna
patient._breed_note: One document token, two schema fields: breed.name and breed.is_mixed. dog.breed_id is nullable by design ('some kind of terrier' is a real answer), so a model that cannot resolve the breed should leave it null rather than guess.
patient._sex_note: Also one token, two fields — dog_sex is an enum of male/female/unknown, so 'spayed female' is not a value it can hold. Contrast the BetterVet certificate, which says only 'SEX: Male': there is_altered must stay NULL, because the absence of the word 'neutered' is not evidence of an intact dog.
patient._dob_note: Stated outright. This is the mirror of BetterVet trap 4 — there the page gave an age and the birth date had to be resisted; here the page gives the birth date and the AGE is what would be derived. Nothing on this page states an age.

clinic.name: Family Pet Hospital
clinic.tagline: Quality affordable PET CARE at your convenience
clinic._website_note: Misspelled on the page as 'FamiliyPetsHospital.com'. Capture verbatim. Do not silently correct it — if the page is ever the evidence in a dispute, what it said matters more than what it meant.

_why_it_matters: The page declares its own staleness. That is a genuine fact about the document
and belongs on the extraction, not on any vaccination record. It is also the
same day the Doc Side email for the other dog was sent, which is a useful
coincidence: both households' records were pulled on one date.
See must_not_produce[1] — this date sits close to the table and is the most
available wrong answer for any missing date field.

_why_this_replaces_v1_vaccinations: The section header on the page reads 'Vaccinations'. Seven of its eleven rows are
not vaccinations. Two are preventative medications, four are diagnostic tests,
one is a deworming treatment. A model that trusts the header produces seven
vaccination records for things that were never vaccines.
This is the single most important property of this document, and it is the whole
argument for document_term.is_vaccine being a positive mapping rather than an
absence: 'Canine Lyme Test' must be POSITIVELY KNOWN not to be a vaccine, or it
returns to the review queue every month forever.
line_items._column_note: Both dates present on every row. Unlike the Doc Side invoice (no expiry) and the Doc Side email (no administration date), this format is complete. It is the easy case for dates and the hard case for classification — a useful inversion to have in the corpus.

rows._validity: 1096 days / 30.4375 = 36.008 -> rounds to 36 -> rabies range [12, 36] -> validity_implausible = false, with one unit of headroom at the top

rows._trap: A Lyme VACCINE exists and is common. This row is a Lyme TEST. One word separates a diagnostic result from an immunisation. See must_not_produce[3].

The hardest row on the page. It is an injection, it has a due date, its interval is a clean six months (183 days / 30.4375 = 6.01), and it sits in a table headed 'Vaccinations'. Everything about its shape says vaccine. It is a slow-release parasiticide. See must_not_produce[2].

rows._validity: 198 days / 30.4375 = 6.505 -> rounds to 7 -> bordetella range [6, 12] -> false
rows._trap: 'Bi-annual' is ambiguous English — twice a year, or every two years. Here the stated dates settle it at roughly six and a half months. A model that resolves the word instead of reading the dates has a fifty-fifty chance of a four-fold error. The dates are stated; no resolution is required.

rows._tracked_note: Recorded but advisory: leptospirosis is seeded regulatory_required = false AND required_by_policy = false, so refresh_dog_vaccine_compliance skips it and it never sets a compliance state. This row exercises the 'recorded but never tracked' branch, which no current test covers.
rows._validity: 365 days / 30.4375 = 11.992 -> rounds to 12 -> leptospirosis range [12, 12] -> false, with ZERO headroom on either side. See schema_gaps[4].
rows._ocr_note: Rendered on the page as 'Leptospirosis 4- Way' with a stray space after the hyphen. Term normalisation must collapse whitespace, or this is a different string from 'Leptospirosis 4-Way'.

rows._validity: 1096 days / 30.4375 = 36.008 -> rounds to 36 -> dhpp range [12, 36] -> false
rows._mapping_is_a_judgement: This names two components (distemper, parvo) of a vaccine your schema calls DHPP (distemper, hepatitis, parainfluenza, parvo). In practice it is the same core combination shot, but the page does not say so. This is exactly the term that should hit needs_review the first time and be mapped once by a human — not guessed by a model, and not hard-coded in a prompt. See vocabulary_decisions[1].

_one_event_many_rows: Rows 2, 3, 4 and 5 share a given date and a due date and are the four results of a
single Accuplex/4DX blood panel — one needle, four lines. Rows 9 and 10 likewise
pair a treatment with its screen on one visit day.
Nothing in the schema needs this today, because none of them become vaccination
records. It matters the moment a visit-level view exists, and it is cheap to note
now while the page is in front of you.

_why: Eleven rows produce eleven document_term entries on first encounter. Ten of the
eleven are unambiguous once a human looks at them; one is a real judgement call.
This section records what the human decided and why, so the same question is not
re-litigated the next time a Petly clinic appears.

terms.reasoning: Names two of four DHPP components. Standard veterinary practice treats 'Distemper/Parvo' as the core combination vaccine, and the three-year adult interval matches. But this is domain inference layered on an incomplete label — precisely a human's call, and worth recording as medium confidence so a later audit can find it.
terms._alternative_considered: A separate 'dapp' vaccine_type. Rejected: it would fragment the compliance ladder across two codes that mean the same obligation, and every clinic names this shot differently.

terms.reasoning: Injectable, but a parasiticide, not an immunisation. Recording it as a vaccine would put a non-vaccine on a health department packet.

The cadence adjective is noise; the vaccine name is unambiguous. Normalisation should strip leading cadence words so 'Bordetella Annual Injectable' from the Doc Side records collapses to the same term.
A Lyme vaccine exists, which is exactly why this needs a positive is_vaccine = false rather than simply being unmapped. Left unmapped it returns to the review queue on every future Petly document.

absent._why_three_categories: v1 needed two — blank-but-labelled versus not-present. This page needs a third: printed form fields that were never filled in. They differ from a blank data field because a human was supposed to answer them and did not, and because on this page the answer is inferable from elsewhere on the same sheet.

labeled_but_blank._note: 'Color:' printed with nothing after it. Same as the BetterVet certificate.

unfilled_form_fields._source_text: Is your pet on a heartworm preventative? [ ] Yes  [ ] No
unfilled_form_fields._note: Neither box ticked. The correct extraction is null — not 'No', and not 'Yes'. See must_not_produce[4], which is the interesting one on this page, because the honest answer is almost certainly 'Yes' and the page still does not say it.

unfilled_form_fields._source_text: If Yes, how often? [ ] Daily  [ ] Monthly  [ ] Other ______
unfilled_form_fields._note: Three unticked boxes and an empty rule. A conditional sub-question of an unanswered question.

not_present._note: Nowhere on the page. See schema_gaps[2] — this is the finding that matters most.
No lot numbers for any of the eleven rows.
No product manufacturers. 'ProHeart-6' is a trade name in the term itself, not a manufacturer field.
Only 'Perry Hall, MD 21128'. City, state and ZIP without a street.
The header clinic is assumed for all eleven rows, but no row states where it was given. For a dog seen at more than one practice this assumption is unsafe.

must_not_produce.source_of_error: 'We fetched this information on Jun 9, 2026' in the page footer
must_not_produce.why_tempting: It is the most recent date on the page and the only one not inside a table cell. For any row where a date is unclear it is the nearest available filler.
must_not_produce._note: As an administered_on it would make several rows implausible and trip the flag; as an expires_on on a row given in 2025 it produces a short but survivable interval. The flag is not a reliable backstop for this error.

must_not_produce.wrong_value: a record for 'ProHeart-6 Heartworm Prevent Inj'
must_not_produce.source_of_error: row 6, under a section header reading 'Vaccinations'
must_not_produce.why_tempting: Injectable, six-month interval, due date, listed among vaccines. Every structural signal says vaccine except the pharmacology.
must_not_produce._what_actually_stops_it: vaccination_record.vaccine_type_id is NOT NULL REFERENCES vaccine_type(id), and there is no row for it — so the insert fails at the foreign key rather than silently creating a bad record. That is the schema working, but it fails as a crash rather than as a review item. The document_term table is what turns it into a clean 'not a vaccine' decision.

must_not_produce.wrong_value: a Lyme vaccination record from 'Canine Lyme Test'
must_not_produce.why_tempting: A canine Lyme vaccine is real and common. Dropping the word 'Test' turns a negative diagnostic result into an immunisation on the dog's record.
must_not_produce._note: Same failure shape as trap 2 but with an important difference: this one inverts the meaning of the underlying event. The test showing the dog does NOT have Lyme becomes a claim that the dog is protected against it.

must_not_produce.source_of_error: row 6 shows a ProHeart-6 injection given 2026-04-29 and due 2026-10-29
must_not_produce.why_tempting: The dog is, in fact, on a heartworm preventative. The evidence is four inches down the same page. The inference is correct and the checkbox is still empty.
_note: The v1 counterpart to this was deriving a birth date from a stated age — an
inference that would also have been right. This one is sharper, because the
supporting evidence is on the same page rather than in outside knowledge.
It is worth being clear about why null is still the right answer: the checkbox
records what the OWNER told the clinic, and the table records what the CLINIC
administered. They are different facts with different provenance, and a form
the owner never filled in is not evidence about what the owner believes. If you
want the inference, make it downstream where it is visible and attributed — not
inside the extraction, where it becomes indistinguishable from something the

must_not_produce.why_tempting: It is what the page says. dog_sex is an enum of male / female / unknown and cannot hold it; the alteration status belongs in dog.is_altered.
must_not_produce._note: One token, two columns. The general shape recurs — 'Shih Tzu Mix' splits the same way into breed.name and breed.is_mixed.

must_not_produce.source_of_error: computed from DOB 2018-07-07 and the fetch date 2026-06-09
must_not_produce.why_tempting: The arithmetic is correct and the inputs are both on the page. But no age appears anywhere on this document, and an age computed against a fetch date is a different fact from an age recorded at a visit.
must_not_produce._note: The exact inverse of BetterVet trap 4, and worth keeping both: one page states an age and tempts you into a birth date, the other states a birth date and tempts you into an age. The rule that survives both is the same one.

must_not_produce.source_of_error: row 1 carries a rabies vaccination with both dates
must_not_produce.why_tempting: It contains the rabies facts a certificate would contain. It is not a certificate: it is unsigned, names no veterinarian, and carries no licence number. See schema_gaps[2].

schema_outcome._why: What the database should hold once a human confirms the extraction.

document.owner_id: <the Marsh household — a different owner from the Jaddi documents>
document._dedupe: The identical second upload must be rejected by UNIQUE (owner_id, sha256). Worth an explicit test — it is the branch the ingestion flow's dedupe logic depends on.

schema_outcome._of_eleven_rows: Seven rows correctly produce nothing. That ratio is the point of this document.
exercises_these_invariants: verification_coherent           — unverified, so verified_by and verified_at both NULL
flag_validity_plausibility      — four rows, four different intervals, none flagged
vaccination_record_dog_idx      — 'latest' is by expires_on, and this dog now has records expiring 2026-11-13, 2026-12-19 and 2028-10-15 across three tracked vaccines
compliance_view_note: As of the fetch date (2026-06-09) this dog reads:
bordetella  expiring_soon  expires 2026-11-13 — inside the 30-day window only after 2026-10-14
leptospirosis — no row at all; not tracked
So the dog rolls up to 'current' at the fetch date. Re-run the same fixture after
2026-11-13 and it becomes 'expired', which makes this document a natural
regression case for the read-time computation: same data, different day, different
answer, with nothing stored that had to be refreshed.

_why_this_section_exists: The BetterVet certificate happened to fit the schema exactly. This one does not.
Four facts on this page have nowhere to live, and the labelling pass is the
cheapest possible moment to find that out — before a pipeline is emitting rows
into a shape that cannot hold them.

gaps.gap: document_class has no value for a portal summary
gaps.detail: The enum is ('form51', 'vet_invoice', 'handwritten_note', 'rabies_certificate', 'unknown'). This page and the Doc Side email are both clinic-generated vaccination summaries — neither an invoice nor a certificate. Both fall to 'unknown', which erases a distinction that matters: how much you should trust a field depends on what kind of document produced it.
gaps.suggested_fix: Add 'vaccination_summary' to document_class. Cheap now; an enum value added later requires touching every place that switches on the class.

gaps.gap: no way to record that a rabies record has no veterinarian attached to it
gaps.detail: vaccination_record.veterinarian_name and veterinarian_license_no are nullable, correctly — a DHPP entry typed in from memory does not need them. But a Maryland rabies certificate does. This page produces a rabies record with no vet, no licence, no lot and no signature, and the schema accepts it as equal in standing to the signed BetterVet certificate. compliance_packet.dogs_missing_records counts dogs with NO record; it cannot see a dog whose record would not survive an inspection.
gaps.why_it_matters: The README's argument is that a compliance packet which silently omits the dogs with no paperwork is worse than no packet, because it reads as an all-clear. A packet that includes a rabies record with no veterinarian on it fails in the same way, one level down.
suggested_fix: Smallest version: a vaccine_type.requires_vet_attribution boolean, and a generated column or view flagging records that are regulatory but unattributed. That flag then feeds compliance_packet alongside dogs_missing_records.

Do NOT make it a hard constraint. Refusing the record would lose the only evidence the shop has, which is the failure mode this whole schema is organised against. Flag it, surface it in the packet, let a human chase the certificate.

gaps.gap: nowhere to store the microchip or the rabies tag number
gaps.detail: dog has no microchip column, and vaccination_record has no tag_number column. This page carries both; the BetterVet certificate carries a tag number too (a differently-formatted one). A rabies tag is a legally referenced identifier — it is the number on the physical tag on the collar.
gaps.why_it_matters: The microchip is the strongest identity key you will ever get for reconciling the same dog across two clinics that spell its name differently. You have exactly the situation that needs it: two households, three practices, and no shared identifier between them today.
gaps.suggested_fix: dog.microchip text with a format CHECK, unique where not null. vaccination_record.tag_number text. Both nullable — plenty of records legitimately have neither.

gaps.gap: the leptospirosis plausibility range has no headroom
gaps.detail: vaccine_type seeds leptospirosis at min 12 and max 12 months. This row lands at 11.992, which rounds to 12 and passes. Anything under roughly 350 days rounds to 11 and trips the flag — and a booster given three weeks early is routine, not suspicious.
gaps.why_it_matters: A flag that fires on ordinary scheduling variance is a flag people learn to ignore, and then it is worth nothing when something is actually wrong.
gaps.suggested_fix: Widen to [10, 14]. The check exists to catch a mis-extracted date by an order of magnitude, not to audit a clinic's calendar.

notes: This is the cleanest document in the corpus for dates and the messiest for classification. The three PDFs are the reverse. Keep both kinds — a corpus where every document is hard in the same way measures one skill and reports it as an average.

Petly is a portal product used across many practices, so this one labelled example generalises further than a practice-specific layout would. If a second Petly clinic ever appears, expect the layout to hold and only the vocabulary to shift.

Nothing here needed OCR-error traps because the screenshot is clean and high-contrast. A photographed page under room light would fail differently, and that gap in the corpus is real — worth capturing one bad photo deliberately rather than waiting for a user to supply one.
